newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria sees CA investment, foreign synergy.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria sees CA investment, foreign synergy.

text.p: Bank Austria, fresh from winning EU approval for its takeover of Creditanstalt, forecast on Monday the deal would bring big synergy gains abroad but said the branch networks would operate independently at home.

Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa said the banks would assume one identity outside Austria "as quickly as possible". They would also work together in investment banking and in the development of new systems and products.

"There is enormous potential for savings. The two banks are spending more than three billion schillings a year in systems development alone. Their parallel development in new markets is costing another three billion," Randa told a news conference.
He forecast synergy effects would be worth around five billion schillings in five years' time but conceded costs would outstrip savings in the first one to two years.
"We expect a burden of a few hundred million schillings in the first one to two years but little of that will be visible in our consolidated results," Randa said.

By bringing together the two banks' investment banking operations the group would reap the benefits of their differing strengths. Creditanstalt Investmentbank had a proven track record in Eastern Europe while Investmentbank Austria's expertise lay in privatisations and flotations.
"By concentrating on the strengths of both institutions we will create a more integrated, more competitive Austrian investment bank in Europe," Randa said.
He said central and eastern Europe would continue to provide the greatest growth potential. He also underlined his commitment to divesting non-financial interests and concentrating on core business.
Randa reiterated there would be no compulsory redundancies or programme of branch closures in Austria.

"It is not a problem to have competition between two brand names with a common owner. It is an everyday occurence," he said, adding that Bank Austria and Creditanstalt would continue to pursue an independent price policy with regard to their customers.
"I see the two brand-name strategy in place for the next five to ten years," he said -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom +43-1 531 12 254
